manifest.name: dsh-workspace-relink
manifest.description: Workspace routing migration for DeepSeek Harness: repoint a workspace at a moved directory, keep its stored sessions usable through a recorded directory junction, and move individual sessions between workspaces.

scripts.check: node --check index.js && node --check client.js && node --check lib/relink.js && node --check lib/routes.js && node --check lib/tool-spec.js

bundle.text:
# dsh-workspace-relink — 工作区路由迁徙
#
# Why this bundle exists: a DSH workspace is one registry record pointing at one
# directory, and a stored session is grouped into that workspace by
# realpath(header.cwd). Move the project folder and both halves stop working:
# the workspace reports missing-dir and the sessions it lists cannot resolve
# their working directory. Session headers are append-only and have no
# relocation API, so this plugin repoints the workspace record at the new
# directory and leaves a directory route (a junction) at the old spelling, then
# transfers session ownership through the registry's own validation. The page
# under Plugins → 工作区路由迁徙 does all of it, and the recorded routes can be
# inspected and removed at any time.
#
# Everything below is the row's default config; the profile patch layer keeps
# user edits across upgrades.
- insert:
    - id: workspace-relink
      name: dsh-workspace-relink
      config:
        agentTools: true
        allowSessionRoutes: true

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Workspace routing migration for DeepSeek Harness.** Move a project folder, then
repoint its workspace at the new location — the conversations that lived in the
old folder keep working, without a single byte of session history being rewritten.

A DSH workspace is one registry record pointing at one directory, and a stored
session is grouped into a workspace by the canonical form of `cwd` recorded in
its immutable header. Move the files and both halves break at once:

- the workspace reports `missing-dir`;
- the conversations it lists cannot resolve their working directory, so every
  tool call fails until the directory is back.

There is no relocation API — the header is append-only storage — so the only
honest fix is to make the old directory *spelling* resolve again while the
workspace record moves to the new canonical path. That is exactly what a
directory route (a Windows directory junction) does, and it is why this plugin is
about **routing**, not about editing history.

```
D:\A\B\C  ──►  moved by you to  ──►  D:\E\F\A\B\C
    │                                     │
    └── becomes a junction ───────────────┘
        (workspace record now lives here)

1. You move the files yourself (this plugin never moves or deletes your data).
2. `工作区路由迁徙` (Plugins → the plugin's page) plans the move: it checks the new
   directory, says whether the old path is free, and lists what it will do.
3. On apply it creates the junction at the old path, creates (or reuses) the
   workspace at the new canonical path, transfers each session's ownership
   through the registry's own attach/detach validation, and retires the old
   registration once nothing is left in it.

The same page can move a **single conversation** into another workspace, and
manages the junctions it created (inspect them, remove them).

- The old and new directories must be reachable from the same machine; a
  junction is a local filesystem object.
- Junction creation needs no elevation on Windows (`fs.symlink(..., 'junction')`).
- A leftover old directory (copy instead of move) blocks the plan until you let
  the plugin rename it aside as `<name>.moved-<timestamp>`; nothing is deleted.
- Removing a junction is allowed only for routes this plugin recorded, and only
  while the path still is a junction. Conversations that resolved their working
  directory through it go back to reporting a missing directory.
- A conversation whose recorded directory is a *different existing directory*
  cannot be re-homed into a workspace it does not resolve to — DSH refuses that
  ownership transfer, and so does this plugin, instead of silently detaching it.
- Sessions whose logs carry no `cwd` are reported as untransferable rather than
  guessed at.

Plugins → 工作区路由迁徙.

- Every workspace with its path, status badge, session count, and expandable
  session list.
- Per workspace: `修改位置` → new path, `浏览…`, `预览计划`, `执行迁徙`, with
  blockers and warnings spelled out before anything is written.
- Per session: move it to another workspace.
- Recorded routes with target liveness and a remove button.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `workspace_relink_status` | Workspaces, paths, status, session counts, recorded routes. `includeSessions: true` also returns each session's id, title, recorded cwd, `cwdState` and `live` flag |
| `workspace_relink_plan` | Dry run for repointing one workspace |
| `workspace_relink_apply` | Execute it (`confirmed: true` required) |
| `workspace_relink_move_session` | Move one conversation into another workspace |
| `workspace_relink_route_remove` | Remove one recorded route |

Every tool answers with a one-line human summary plus the full JSON payload as a
second text block, so the model can read `plan.blockers[].code`, workspace ids and
session titles instead of guessing from prose.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agentTools` | `true` | Expose the tools above to the model; the page always works |
| `allowSessionRoutes` | `true` | Allow creating a route when moving a conversation whose directory is gone |

Routes this plugin created are recorded in
`<DSH_HOME>/workspace-relink/routes.json` (absolute paths, kind, ids, timestamp).
It is an index over the filesystem, never the authority: a hand-made symlink is
never touched, and a recorded route whose link is gone is simply reported.

```
node scripts/selftest.mjs
```

The harness exercises the engine against a stand-in registry that reproduces
DSH's membership canon (`realpath(header.cwd)` equality, plus the missing-cwd
wildcard): broken state, plan, apply, route reuse, refusal cases, leftover
directory displacement, single-session adoption, and route removal. It writes
nothing outside a temporary directory.
